questions.stem: I’d just arrived at school, ready for another school day. I was reading a book in the classroom when there was an announcement. “Today at 1: 10 there will be auditions (面试) for a musical.” My friends all jumped up in excitement and asked me, “Will you be going, Amy?” “Sure,” I said. I had no ___2___ in drama, but I’d try out because my friends were doing it.
questions.analysis: 本题考查名词词义辨析及上下文逻辑理解。题干中，作者在朋友邀请参加音乐剧面试时表示“Sure”，但随后提到“I had no ___ in drama”，结合后文“but I’d try out because my friends were doing it”可知，作者对戏剧本身没有兴趣，只是因为朋友参加才尝试。选项A. hesitancy（犹豫）与后文“but I’d try out”矛盾，因为如果无犹豫，则无需转折；选项B. interest（兴趣）符合语境，表示“对戏剧没有兴趣”；选项C. worry（担心）与后文“try out”无直接逻辑关系；选项D. regret（后悔）不符合前文“Sure”的积极态度。解题思路：通过上下文转折关系“but”判断前后语义相反，前文说“Sure”表示同意，后文解释原因时需体现缺乏内在动机，故“no interest”最合理。语法点：名词短语“no interest in”为固定搭配，表示“对……没有兴趣”。

questions.stem: At 1:10, there was a ___3___ outside the drama room. Everyone looked energetic. I hadn’t expected I’d be standing there that morning. But now that I was doing it, I ___4___ felt nervous. What if I wasn’t any good?
questions.analysis: 本题考查名词词义辨析及语境理解。题干描述戏剧室外的场景，关键词为'drama room'（戏剧室）和'everyone looked energetic'（每个人看起来精力充沛），暗示与戏剧表演相关。选项A. game（游戏、比赛）不符合戏剧语境；B. show（演出、展示）虽与表演相关，但通常指大型演出或电视节目，不如'play'具体；C. play（戏剧、剧本）直接对应'drama room'，指戏剧表演；D. line（队伍、台词）中'line'可指排队，但后文'everyone looked energetic'暗示表演即将开始，而非排队。结合上下文，'there was a play outside the drama room'意为戏剧室外面有一场戏剧表演，符合逻辑。解题思路：抓住关键词'drama room'，排除无关选项，选择最符合戏剧场景的'play'。

questions.stem: What is moderation (适度)? Basically, it means eating only as much food as your body needs. You should feel satisfied at the end of a meal, but not too full. ____16____ But it doesn't mean saying goodbye to the foods you love.
options: A. Eat properly throughout the day.
B. We don't always eat just to satisfy hunger.
C. Don't swallow a meal on the way to work.
D. Most of us need to double the amount we eat.
E. Instead, surround yourself with healthy choices.
F. For many of us, moderation means eating less than we do now.
G. That won't lead to cheating or giving up on your new eating plan.
questions.analysis: 本题考查上下文逻辑。前文解释了适度的含义，后文转折说并不意味着告别喜欢的食物，因此F选项“对许多人来说，适度意味着比现在吃得少”符合语境。

questions.stem: What does the author intend to do by challenging a hypothesis?
questions.analysis: 本题考察对作者写作意图的理解，涉及词汇和逻辑推理。题干中“challenging a hypothesis”意为“质疑一个假设”，其中“challenge”作动词表示“质疑、挑战”，“hypothesis”是“假设、假说”。选项A“Make an assumption”意为“做出假设”，与题干“质疑”矛盾；选项B“Illustrate an argument”意为“阐明一个论点”，质疑假设通常是为了支持或阐述自己的论点，符合逻辑；选项C“Give a suggestion”意为“提出建议”，与质疑假设无关；选项D“Justify a comparison”意为“证明比较的合理性”，题干未涉及比较。解题思路：理解“challenge a hypothesis”的常见写作目的，即通过质疑现有观点来引出或加强自己的论证。因此，正确答案为B。

questions.stem: What does the phrase “contingent on” underlined in Paragraph 2 probably mean?
questions.analysis: 本题考查短语含义推断。题干要求解释第二段中划线短语“contingent on”的意思。根据词汇知识，“contingent on”意为“取决于，视……而定”，与“determined by”（由……决定）含义相近。选项A“Accepted by”（被接受）不符合；选项C“Awakened by”（被唤醒）和D“Discovered by”（被发现）均与语境无关。解题时需结合上下文理解短语逻辑关系，通常“contingent on”表示条件依赖关系。因此正确答案为B。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the forming of the Inuit’s moral code?
options: A. Living conditions were the drive.
B. Unwritten rules were the target.
C. Social tradition was the basis.
questions.analysis: 本题为推断题，考查对文本隐含信息的理解。题干询问关于因纽特人道德准则形成的推断。根据原文，因纽特人生活在极端恶劣的环境中，生存条件艰苦，因此他们的道德准则（如诚实、互助）是为了适应环境、确保群体生存而形成的。选项A“生活条件是驱动力”符合这一逻辑。选项B“不成文规则是目标”因果倒置，规则是结果而非目标；选项C“社会传统是基础”虽有一定道理，但传统本身源于生存需求；选项D“诚实是关键”过于片面，且未涉及形成原因。解题思路：抓住题干关键词“forming”（形成），寻找原文中关于道德准则起源的线索，通常与生存环境相关。语法点：infer（推断）要求基于文本证据进行逻辑推理，而非直接引用。

questions.stem: 根据短文内容，从短文后的七个选项中选出能填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。If you want to develop maximum credibility (可信性), is it better to be a hedgehog (刺猬) or a fox? According to Isaiah Berlin, the hedgehog knows one thing very well, and the fox knows a lot of things.Is there a clear advantage of one style over the other? Hedgehog thinkers tend to answer yes. ___35___ And they are usually very credible in doing so. According to Jim Hart, the “hedgehog concept” is one of the factors that lead companies to greatness. They focus on one thing and do it really well. They figure out what they are good at. ___36___ The hedgehog concept makes perfect sense for companies.___37___ Philip Tate has studied the track records of those folks on the Sunday talk shows who make predictions about what will happen. He has found that hedgehogs are not only wrong more often than foxes, but that they are less likely to recognise or admit that they are wrong when events do not match their predictions.The advantage that foxes have is that they are more likely to seek out new information from a broader range of sources, and are comfortable with uncertainty and new information. ___38___ They try to include it in their viewpoint rather than to exclude it from their thinking. They also have a clearer estimation of what they know and don’t know.So, which is better? The question can be answered in a foxy hedgehog style. ___39___ The choice between being a hedgehog or a fox is a false trade-off. The most effective way to go through life is to try to be that rare mixture known as foxy hedgehog.A. In other words, there are clear advantages for each.B. They are more likely to remember people’s mistakes.C. Hence, they have the advantage of clarity and confidence.D. But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing.E. However, hedgehogs remain open to others’ reactions and inputs.F. When something is contradictory to their view, they don’t treat it as exceptional.G. They come down squarely on one side or t
options: A. In other words, there are clear advantages for each.
B. They are more likely to remember people’s mistakes.
C. Hence, they have the advantage of clarity and confidence.
D. But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing.
E. However, hedgehogs remain open to others’ reactions and inputs.
F. When something is contradictory to their view, they don’t treat it as exceptional.
G. They come down squarely on one side or the other and fully support their position.
questions.analysis: 本文讨论刺猬型（专注单一领域）与狐狸型（知识广博）思维方式的优劣。解题需根据上下文逻辑和关键词判断。**35题**：前文说刺猬型思想家倾向于回答“是”，后文说他们这样做时通常非常可信。G选项“他们明确站在一边并全力支持自己的立场”承接前文“回答是”，并引出后文“可信”，形成因果逻辑。**36题**：前文提到刺猬型专注于一件事并做得很好，C选项“因此，他们具有清晰和自信的优势”总结前文，说明专注带来的好处，符合逻辑。**37题**：前文讲刺猬型对公司的好处，后文转折讲其缺点（预测错误且不认错）。D选项“但专注于一件大事可能有缺点”引出下文，形成对比。**38题**：前文说狐狸型善于接受新信息，后文说他们试图将矛盾信息纳入观点。F选项“当某事与他们的观点相矛盾时，他们不将其视为例外”具体描述狐狸型处理矛盾的方式，与后文“纳入观点”一致。**39题**：前文问“哪个更好”，后文说选择是虚假的权衡，最佳方式是混合型。A选项“换句话说，每种方式都有明显优势”总结前文，引出后文对混合型的推崇。**语法与词汇**：- “come down squarely on one side”意为“明确站在一边”，固定搭配。- “downside”意为“缺点、不利方面”，与“advantage”相对。- “contradictory to”意为“与……矛盾”，后接名词。- “exceptional”意为“例外的”，此处指不视为特殊。**解题思路**：七选五需关注代词（如they指代前文主语）、逻辑连接词（如hence、but、however）和内容连贯性。先读选项，再回原文找线索，排除多余选项（本题多余选项为B和E）。

They focus on one thing and do it really well. They figure out what they are good at. ___36___ The hedgehog concept makes perfect sense for companies.___37___ Philip Tate has studied the track records of those folks on the Sunday talk shows who make predictions about what will happen. He has found that hedgehogs are not only wrong more often than foxes, but that they are less likely to recognise or admit that they are wrong when events do not match their predictions.The advantage that foxes have is that they are more likely to seek out new information from a broader range of sources, and are comfortable with uncertainty and new information. ___38___ They try to include it in their viewpoint rather than to exclude it from their thinking. They also have a clearer estimation of what they know and don’t know.So, which is better? The question can be answered in a foxy hedgehog style. ___39___ The choice between being a hedgehog or a fox is a false trade-off. options: A. In other words, there are clear advantages for each.
B. They are more likely to remember people’s mistakes.
C. Hence, they have the advantage of clarity and confidence.
D. But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing.
E. However, hedgehogs remain open to others’ reactions and inputs.
F. When something is contradictory to their view, they don’t treat it as exceptional.
G. They come down squarely on one side or the other and fully support their position.
questions.analysis: 这是一道七选五阅读理解题，考查考生对上下文逻辑关系和语篇连贯性的理解。解题思路：首先通读全文，把握文章主旨——比较刺猬型（专注单一）和狐狸型（广博灵活）思维方式的优劣。然后分析每个空白处的上下文，寻找逻辑衔接词和指代关系。- 第35空：前文说“Hedgehog thinkers tend to answer yes”，后文说“And they are usually very credible in doing so”，说明刺猬型思维者会明确支持自己的立场。选项G“They come down squarely on one side or the other and fully support their position”符合逻辑，指代“they”即刺猬型思维者，且与后文“credible”呼应。- 第36空：前文说“They focus on one thing and do it really well. They figure out what they are good at”，强调刺猬型的优势。选项C“Hence, they have the advantage of clarity and confidence”是因果关系，总结前文，说明他们因此拥有清晰和自信的优势。- 第37空：后文提到Philip Tate的研究发现刺猬型更常犯错且不愿承认，这是对刺猬型专注单一可能带来的负面影响的转折。选项D“But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing”引出下文，符合转折逻辑。- 第38空：前文说狐狸型善于从广泛来源获取新信息，后文说“They try to include it in their viewpoint rather than to exclude it from their thinking”，说明他们对待矛盾信息的态度。选项F“When something is contradictory to their view, they don’t treat it as exceptional”具体描述这种态度，与后文一致。- 第39空：前文问“which is better?”，后文说“The choice between being a hedgehog or a fox is a false trade-off”，暗示两者各有优势。选项A“In other words, there are clear advantages for each”总结前文，引出后文关于“foxy hedgehog”混合体的结论。语法点：考查连接词（hence, but, however）、代词指代（they）、逻辑关系（因果、转折、并列）。词汇用法：downside（缺点）、contradictory（矛盾的）、exceptional（例外的）、trade-off（权衡）。

questions.stem: 阅读下面短文，根据题目要求用英文回答问题。Growing up, I idealised independence. I always wanted my own efforts to be enough. When I decided to pursue a postgraduate degree, I wanted to develop a novel research programme and quickly establish myself as an independent scientist. But I was unrealistically optimistic about what I could achieve.As I began designing experiments, my committee members warned me about the challenges I would face. But my need for independence drove me to push forward with my research plan. As a result, the first four years of my postgraduate career were defined by a series of failures.During my second year, I failed my comprehensive exam because my proposal was unclear. During my third year, I discovered that after treating thousands of seeds, I obtained just one plant I could use for experiments. By my fourth year, my desperation to succeed overshadowed my desire for independence.My adviser and I devised (想出) a somewhat unusual solution: I would spend three months in a collaborating (合作的) lab to obtain specialised training. I worked extensively with other students, constantly asked questions, and helped with ongoing projects to learn everything I could. Finally, I conducted an elegant experiment that would not have been possible without the help of the members in the lab.My adviser saw this experience as a groundbreaking success, emphasising the collaborating skills I acquired. A few months later, when I repeated the experiment in my home lab, I produced more publishable data. By learning when to ask for help, I eventually found myself on the way to becoming an independent scientist.
questions.answer: The author learned that true independence in science comes from knowing when to ask for help and collaborate with others, rather than relying solely on one's own efforts.
questions.analysis: 本题为阅读理解题，要求概括短文主旨。文章讲述作者从追求完全独立到认识到合作重要性的成长过程。语法点：一般过去时描述经历，现在完成时强调影响。词汇用法：'idealised'（理想化）、'unrealistically optimistic'（不切实际地乐观）、'groundbreaking success'（突破性成功）。解题思路：通读全文，抓住转折点——作者从失败到成功的转变源于接受合作。答案应体现'ask for help'和'collaboration'是成为独立科学家的关键。

questions.answer: Dear Jim,I'm glad to hear that you're planning to write for the Asia Today column. Since this year marks the 75th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, I suggest you focus on China's remarkable achievements in areas like economy, technology, and infrastructure. For example, you could mention the rapid development of high-speed railways, the success of the Belt and Road Initiative, and advancements in 5G technology. These topics are not only impressive but also well-documented, making your article credible and engaging. Additionally, you might include stories about poverty alleviation and environmental protection, as they show China's commitment to sustainable development. I believe these suggestions will help your readers gain a deeper understanding of China's progress.Yours,Li Hua

questions.stem: Please decide which part is false in the following statement, then underline it and explain why.> The adviser considered the author’s experience in the lab a groundbreaking success because publishable data had been produced.
questions.analysis: 该题考查句子结构和逻辑关系。原句中'because publishable data had been produced'是原因状语从句，但主句'considered...a groundbreaking success'中的宾语补足语结构为'consider + 宾语 + 宾语补足语'，通常用形容词或名词短语作补足语，而这里'groundbreaking success'是名词短语，语法正确。然而，逻辑上，'publishable data had been produced'（已产生可发表的数据）作为原因，与'groundbreaking success'（突破性成功）不匹配，因为产生可发表的数据通常只是研究过程中的一个步骤，不足以构成突破性成功。因此，错误部分在于原因从句，应改为更合理的原因，如'because the data led to a major discovery'。语法点：原因状语从句的时态和逻辑一致性；词汇用法：'groundbreaking'意为'突破性的'，'publishable'意为'可发表的'；解题思路：识别句子结构，检查主从句逻辑关系是否合理。

questions.stem: From this story, what can you learn about “independence”? (In about 40 words)
questions.answer: Independence means the ability to make decisions and take actions on your own, without relying on others. It involves self-reliance and responsibility for one's own life.
questions.analysis: 本题为阅读理解中的开放性问题，要求根据故事内容概括‘independence’的含义。解题思路：首先回顾故事中主人公如何展现独立（如自己解决问题、不依赖他人），然后提炼核心概念。语法点：使用一般现在时描述普遍意义；词汇用法：independence（独立）、self-reliance（自力更生）、responsibility（责任）。答题方法：紧扣故事细节，用简洁语言总结，控制在40词左右。

questions.answer: Dear Jim,I'm glad to hear that you're planning to write about China's development achievements for the Asia Today column. Here are my suggestions.First, you could focus on China's rapid economic growth, such as the Belt and Road Initiative and the rise of high-tech industries like 5G and high-speed rail. Second, you might mention social progress, including poverty alleviation and improved living standards. Third, environmental achievements like the development of renewable energy and green technologies are also worth highlighting.The reason for these suggestions is that they represent the most remarkable and widely recognized aspects of China's progress over the past 75 years. They are not only impressive but also relevant to your readers, as they show how China has contributed to global development and cooperation.I hope these ideas are helpful. Good luck with your article!Yours,Li Hua
questions.analysis: 本题为应用文写作，要求回复邮件，提出建议并说明理由。语法点包括：时态（一般现在时、现在完成时）、情态动词（could, might）、非谓语动词（如'to hear'不定式作原因状语）。词汇用法：'focus on'（聚焦于）、'such as'（例如）、'highlight'（强调）、'represent'（代表）、'relevant to'（与……相关）。解题思路：首先明确写作目的（回复建议），然后分点列出建议内容（经济、社会、环境），最后简要说明理由（代表性、相关性）。注意词数限制和格式（开头结尾已给出）。难度适中，需注意逻辑连贯和语言得体。
